programme: HBP1, SIN3B, DNMT1, NCOR1, KDM5C, ZMYND8 and PHF20 form an HDAC-recruiting chromatin-corepressor network: SIN3B and NCOR1 are the core HDAC-tethering scaffolds (SIN3B represses DREAM-complex cell-cycle targets and cooperates with APC/C for mitotic exit; NCOR1/HDAC3 silences nuclear-receptor and MYBL2-linked targets), HBP1 is an HMG-box repressor that shuts off CCND1/RB1-pathway genes to force cell-cycle exit, DNMT1 provides the DNA-methylation layer that locks these loci silent, and KDM5C/ZMYND8/PHF20 are the chromatin readers/erasers (H3K4 demethylation, dual-mark reading, methyl-mark sensing) that decommission active enhancers and stabilize the repressive state. Together this is a cell-cycle-exit-and-enhancer-silencing module, not a single-pathway signal.
role_in_a: In glioblastoma this network keeps glioma cells out of a differentiated, growth-arrested state: HBP1 restrains RB/CCND1-driven proliferation, SIN3B represses DREAM-complex targets to block mitotic exit, DNMT1 locks silencing in place and is co-opted for CD47-mediated immune evasion and temozolomide resistance (via DNMT1/ELK1), KDM5C shapes a hypoxia-adapted chromatin state and drives SIX5/UBE2C-dependent progression, ZMYND8 is epigenetically rewired in IDH-mutant glioma, and PHF20 promotes malignancy through a WISP1/BGN-dependent invasion programme.
role_in_b: In lung cancer the same corepressor logic is used more narrowly but concretely: DNMT1 dysregulation silences tumor-suppressor/differentiation loci (shown directly in NSCLC and pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma), and NCoR1 acts as a repressive nuclear hub — disrupting RARα/NCoR1 blocks chaperone-mediated autophagy, and DLK1 relocalizes NCoR1 in NSCLC nuclei to alter its repressive output. KDM5C, ZMYND8 and PHF20 are implicated mainly through pan-cancer/general reviews rather than lung-specific mechanistic papers.
shared_axis: Both glioblastoma and lung cancer are proliferative solid tumors that depend on keeping RB/DREAM-complex cell-cycle-exit genes and differentiation-associated enhancers switched off; reusing the same HDAC-scaffold-plus-chromatin-reader toolkit (SIN3B/NCoR1 for tethering, DNMT1 for durable silencing, KDM5C/ZMYND8/PHF20 for enhancer decommissioning) is a generic way to hold that state in any tissue of origin, which is why the same module recurs across independently profiled glial and lung patient groups even though no paper states the two diseases share it.
reasoning: Each carrying factor is independently placed by primary literature in at least one of the two diseases (HBP1 and DNMT1 in both; SIN3B, KDM5C, ZMYND8, PHF20 in glioblastoma; NCOR1 in lung), and the module — an HDAC-corepressor/DREAM-silencing/enhancer-decommissioning network — is nameable from the factors' documented biochemistry alone. The lung-cancer side rests more heavily on DNMT1 and NCoR1 plus general pan-cancer reviews for KDM5C/PHF20/ZMYND8, so the joint claim is a reasoned extension of separately documented biology rather than a stated fact about this pair, which is why it is supported rather than established.
support: PMID 35941115 (HBP1, both diseases — PRMT1 methylation of HBP1 drives tumor progression in glioma and lung tumor cells); PMID 29355710 (HBP1 in glioblastoma — AKT phosphorylation regulates HBP1 activity and glioma proliferation); PMID 30683982 (HBP1 as an HMG-box cell-cycle inhibitor at the crossroads of cancer signaling); PMID 37406020 (HBP1 promotes ferroptosis via UHRF1-CDO1 in lung tumor cells); PMID 30517867 (SIN3B represses DREAM-complex targets and cooperates with APC/C, the mechanistic basis for the cell-cycle-exit arm); PMID 37314748 (chromatin-associated SIN3B protects cancer cells from genotoxic-stress apoptosis); PMID 22895069 (SIN3B/Mad4 regulation dissected in glioblastoma, noted to also touch lung); PMID 42667153 (DNMT1/GSK3β signaling upregulates CD47 for immune evasion in glioblastoma); PMID 40886022 (disrupting DNMT1/ELK1 restores temozolomide sensitivity in glioblastoma); PMID 42652194 (DNMT1/PTEN regulation in NSCLC); PMID 41854102 (altered DNMT1 expression in pulmonary large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma); PMID 40490560 (RARα/NCoR1 disruption blocks chaperone-mediated autophagy in cancer, lung-derived); PMID 31661545 (DLK1 relocalizes NCOR1 in NSCLC nuclei); PMID 41939887 (KDM5C-regulated SIX5 drives glioblastoma progression); PMID 36142158 (KDM5C tied to hypoxia-related signatures in glioma); PMID 41013520 (KDM5 demethylases in therapeutic resistance across cancers, general review touching both diseases); PMID 36692427 (ZMYND8 epigenetically rewired in IDH-mutant glioma); PMID 33117706 (PHF20 promotes glioblastoma malignancy via WISP1/BGN); PMID 39802118 (PHF20 functions reviewed generally, touching both diseases).
how_to_falsify: Perform CUT&RUN/ChIP-seq for SIN3B, NCoR1 and HBP1 in matched glioblastoma and NSCLC lines to test whether they co-occupy the same RB/DREAM-target promoters (CCND1, RB1, MYBL2); then co-deplete SIN3B, NCoR1, DNMT1, KDM5C and ZMYND8 in both lines and check whether the same class of genes (cell-cycle-exit genes and previously silenced enhancers) is derepressed in a matched way. If the factors do not co-occupy the predicted loci, or if knockdown derepresses non-overlapping gene sets between the two tumor types, the shared-module account fails.
caveats: Brain-lung is an anatomically unrelated tissue pairing, so any shared axis must be a generic proliferative/epigenetic mechanism rather than tissue physiology; 224 patient-group comparisons across only 2 independent cohort pairs give reasonable depth but limited cohort diversity. Even the best-supported factor, HBP1, agrees in only 137/224 (61%) of comparisons, so this is a majority-consensus core, not a universal signature — support drops to ~85/224 (38%) for the weakest carrying factors (KDM5C, PHF20, ZMYND8, SIN3B), meaning the account rests on the more strongly supported members (HBP1, DNMT1, NCoR1) more than the weaker ones. EWSR1, YAP1, BCL6, SMAD5 and MYOG were concordant too but excluded from the programme: EWSR1's evidence is mostly fusion-sarcoma-specific and mechanistically distinct (RNA-binding/coactivator, not repressive chromatin); YAP1 is a Hippo-pathway transcriptional activator; BCL6 represses immune/inflammatory rather than cell-cycle genes; SMAD5 is BMP/TGF-β signaling; MYOG has no disease-specific evidence at all — including them would have diluted a coherent story into an unfocused one. The tissue-generic exclusion list notably removed SOX10, the obvious glial/lung master regulator, confirming its absence here reflects the exclusion filter, not an oversight.
